title: Examining the Impact of Residential Density on Household Vehicle Use and Fuel Consumption
abstract: This study investigates the relationship between residential density and household vehicle use and fuel consumption. By employing a simultaneous equation model, we account for self-selection effects to accurately estimate the influence of density on transportation energy use. The results reveal that lower residential density directly increases annual vehicle mileage by approximately 4.8% and leads to an increase in fuel consumption by about 5.5%. This effect is decomposed into two pathways: increased mileage resulting from reduced fuel economy, and a direct impact of density on the efficiency of the household's vehicle fleet.
